about:
AGS-Electronics Manufacturing operates as the electronics division of AGS-TECH Inc., a global industrial supplier and integrator, and is based in Albuquerque, New Mexico. The company does not disclose its founding year or ownership structure in the provided materials.

The business supplies a broad catalog of electronic components — including interconnect hardware, wire and cable assemblies, printed circuit boards and PCB assemblies, electromechanical devices, power conversion modules, motors, sensors, displays, and enclosures — and complements off-the-shelf sales with custom manufacturing, assembly, and integration services. Its service portfolio spans product finding and locating, prototyping, product modification, contract manufacturing, electronics manufacturing outsourcing, engineering integration, and global consolidation, logistics, and supply chain management. The company notes that it leverages low-cost engineering and manufacturing resources in Southeast Asia to support client projects.

AGS-Electronics serves customers across the electronics sector who need prototypes, sub-assemblies, full assemblies, or finished products, though the input does not name specific industries or client examples.

The company states that its distinguishing feature is the breadth of its electronics manufacturing and engineering services, which it contrasts with competitors that offer limited custom capabilities. It emphasizes flexible engineering engagement models and the cost and agility benefits of outsourcing engineering and manufacturing to its network.

name: AGT Foods USA
old_description: is a leading manufacturer of plant-based ingredients for premium markets and
about:
AGT Foods USA operates its ingredient production facility in Minot, North Dakota, as part of the global AGT Food and Ingredients Inc. The company, majority owned by Fairfax Financial Holdings Limited, traces its roots to a mission of providing clean, quality pulses and foodstuffs with reliable shipments and competitive pricing. While a specific founding year is not disclosed, the guiding principle "From Producer to the World" has shaped its growth into a diversified food company.

The Minot facility is one of two North American ingredient plants (the other in Regina, Saskatchewan) that clean, size, split, colour-sort, and package pulses and grains. The company runs 39 manufacturing facilities across five continents, producing over 1,400 products including flours, proteins, starches, fibres, extruded texturized plant proteins, gluten-free pasta, wheat semolina, rice, and bulgur wheat. It also offers co-packing, custom blends, and private-label production for retail brands such as Arbella, PastaVilla, Veggipasta, CLIC, and Tamam.

AGT Foods serves global packaged-food manufacturers, international retailers, and food-service channels, supplying plant-based ingredients and finished goods to 127 countries. Its integrated origination network buys crops directly from producers near its facilities in Canada, the United States, Türkiye, Australia, and South Africa, then processes and exports them through rail and port logistics partnerships.

The company emphasizes vertical integration—capturing value in the communities where crops are grown—and logistical advantages through bulk grain-handling agreements that connect Western Canadian farms to major railways and ports. Its Veggi line of 100% plant-based pastas, breadings, and meal kits exemplifies its focus on innovative, consumer-ready products.

name: ALPLA
old_description: Specializes in custom HDPE packaging for home and personal care
about:
ALPLA, headquartered in Salt Lake City, Utah, is a family-owned plastic packaging manufacturer with a history spanning over 70 years. The company operates 17 high-capacity plants across the United States, including facilities in Jefferson City, Missouri, and Bowling Green, Kentucky, and more than 200 sites globally.

The company produces custom and standardized bottles, closures, and containers for home care, personal care, and industrial applications. Its capabilities include injection molding, large-volume bottle production with dual-neck options, decoration services for private-label and white-label packaging, and in-house testing for sealing, filling, and stacking performance. Plants are equipped for efficient mold and color changeovers, supporting flexible capacities from small runs to large-scale orders.

ALPLA serves brands in home care, personal care, and industrial sectors that require sustainable packaging solutions such as PET, HDPE, rPET, and post-consumer resin (PCR). Customers include companies seeking to localize supply chains, reduce transportation emissions, and accelerate time-to-market through standard designs that eliminate development delays.

The company emphasizes its family-owned heritage, quality and service excellence, and a localized production model that leverages a global network of over 200 facilities. It offers a CO2 reduction calculator to quantify environmental benefits and positions its standard packaging as ready-to-fill, customizable through decoration, color, and closure choices.

about:
AMD is headquartered in Santa Clara, California, and was founded in 1969 as a semiconductor designer and manufacturer. The company began by developing integrated circuits and has grown into a major supplier of processing solutions for computing and graphics.

The company designs and produces central processing units (CPUs), graphics processing units (GPUs), and accelerated processing units (APUs) that combine CPU and GPU functions. Its products serve personal computers, servers, and gaming consoles. AMD employs between 2,000 and 4,999 people across its operations.

AMD serves the PC, gaming, and data center industries. Its technologies are used by businesses and companies for artificial intelligence, embedded, and edge applications. The company highlights partnerships with major enterprises to solve complex computing challenges.

AMD differentiates itself by offering a broad portfolio of AI solutions spanning CPU, GPU, and adaptive computing, an open ecosystem approach based on open standards and co-innovation, and proven leadership in innovation delivering total cost of ownership and efficiency across data center, edge, and endpoint deployments.

about:
AMETEK Level Measurement Solutions (LMS) operates from Naugatuck, Connecticut, as the level and flow measurement division of AMETEK. The unit focuses on designing and producing instrumentation for process industries.

The product portfolio includes displacer transmitters such as the SIL 2‑certified E4 Modulevel®, guided‑wave radar transmitters like the Eclipse® Model 706 (also built in Dubai for hygienic applications), non‑contact radar models such as the Pulsar® R80, and the Genesis™ multiphase detector for emulsion layers. The company also supplies RF admittance switches and provides global service, training, and retrofit programs for existing displacer assemblies.

Customers span process industries including oil and gas, chemical, pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and life sciences, as well as renewable energy. AMETEK LMS sells through a network of local representatives and channel partners; recent agreements named TechStar LLC as exclusive partner for Oklahoma and a new Midwest‑region partnership.

The division emphasizes operational efficiency, safety, and high performance, positioning itself as a preferred partner for process control. Its differentiators include patented TDR‑based multiphase detection and hygienic designs that meet CIP/SIP cleanability requirements with a 15 Ra surface finish.

about:
APCO Plastics operates from Greenville, South Carolina, and was founded in 1996. With over 30 years in the plastics trade, the company provides custom fabrication and CNC routing services to business and personal clients. No founders or ownership structure are disclosed publicly.

The shop’s capabilities include custom fabrication, CNC routing, project design, bending, polishing, and custom light lenses. Its product portfolio spans custom-made turntable dust covers, acrylic lenses, windshields, intubation shields produced for local healthcare during the pandemic, and custom privacy shields. Facility size, headcount, and production volumes are not published.

APCO serves healthcare providers, retail businesses, automotive and motorcycle owners, lighting manufacturers, and hobbyists restoring vintage turntables. Concrete examples from the company’s site include retail displays, replacement windshields, and dust covers for vintage turntables, alongside the COVID-era intubation shields for local health care.

The company highlights a personalized approach, assisting customers with design and material selection, and points to its self-described largest and most loyal customer base in the Upstate as evidence of repeat business. Product excellence and a broad variety of products and services are stated priorities.

about:
ARCH Hawaii operates from a fabrication studio in Honolulu, Hawaii. The company describes itself as a local team of designers, builders, artists, and problem-solvers rooted in Hawai'i, though no founding year or individual founders are disclosed in the available materials. Ownership structure is not specified.

The shop runs 3-axis CNC and CNC foam machining equipment to produce scenic fabrication, set construction, prop fabrication, custom millwork, kinetic sculpture, and public art installations. Work spans materials including wood (notably koa), metal (stainless steel 316 mirror polish), foam, and integrated LED lighting. The facility handles projects from tabletop scale up to two-story installations, offering concept development, production design, CAD, and 3D renderings through its creative studio, plus delivery, rigging, site coordination, and strike services.

Clients come from film and television production (Netflix, NCIS), commercial advertising (LEGO, Nike, Louis Vuitton, The Macallan), retail design (Bank of Hawaii, Meta Lab, Le Monde, Soho House), public art and museums (Hawaii Contemporary, Mission Houses Museum), live entertainment (Cirque du Soleil 'Auana), and corporate branding (Amazon, NBC, MTV, Pandora, The North Face). Broadcast work runs on IATSE union crews built to camera tolerance on fixed schedules.

The company positions its differentiator as combining local Hawaiian craftsmanship with creative thinking and hands-on problem solving to "build what others only imagine," emphasizing a concept-through-installation workflow under one roof, union-qualified crews for broadcast, and island-sourced, eco-conscious materials.

name: ARKK Food Company
old_description: ARKK specializes in identifying a need in the market and bringing unique products to market to fulfill that need.
about:
ARKK Food Company operates from Bloomfield Township, Michigan, where it has spent more than a decade developing, acquiring, and representing transformative food brands. The company was built on the premise of identifying unmet market needs and bringing unique products to market to fulfill them, though a specific founding year and founder names are not publicly disclosed.

The company manages a portfolio of seven brands spanning protein, hydration, and prepared foods. Its Pennsylvania Food Corp division runs a high-volume food manufacturing and assembly facility that produces sandwiches, breakfast bowls, entrée bowls, and handles packaging. Other brands include Wahlburgers for retail burgers, Sonoma Grille for premium ham, Skinny Butcher for double-breaded chicken, Simply Essentials for Black Angus beef, Maple 3 for maple water, and Envisible for supply-chain visibility technology. ARKK reports its products are stocked in over 12,000 retail locations nationwide, and its Farm to Family Grant program has distributed 14.5 million food boxes and sourced 43.5 million pounds of produce from eight states since May 2020.

ARKK serves the retail grocery channel, supplying the largest U.S. retailers, and partners with government and nonprofit relief programs such as the Farm to Family Grant. Its customer base includes national retail chains, food-service distributors, and consumers seeking premium, sustainable protein and beverage options.

The company says it differentiates itself by blending creativity and strategy to craft iconic brands, elevating traditional food items through innovation, and providing end-to-end solutions from product development and sustainability consulting to traceability and consumer engagement.

name: AROS Group - Luxury Packaging
old_description: At AROS Group (Formerly JUJIN NY), every packaging piece is a surface of expression, designed to speak without words.
about:
AROS Group, formerly known as JUJIN NY, operates as a luxury packaging manufacturer headquartered in New York, New York. The company maintains a global presence with offices in Paris, Milan, London, Dubai, Shenzhen, Shanghai, São Paulo, Mexico City, and Singapore, and describes its manufacturing footprint as an integrated network of factories spanning Paris, Shanghai, Milan, and New York. No founding year, ownership structure, or founders are disclosed in the available information.

The company designs and produces multi-material luxury packaging for sectors including fragrance, beauty, spirits and beverages, fashion and accessories, watches and jewelry, haute gastronomy, technology and smart living, and corporate gifting. Its capabilities cover the full lifecycle from concept and prototyping through manufacturing and supply chain coordination, working with materials such as paper, board, fabric, wood, plastics, metal, glass, and composites. AROS Group states it handles both small series and mass production, orchestrating projects through a six-phase process it calls Intuition, Creation, Materialization, Development, Excellence, and Realization.

Clients are primarily luxury brands seeking complete packaging ecosystems — glass bottles, caps, boxes, cases, and accessories — that extend brand rituals. The company cites work across fragrance cases, beauty packaging ecosystems, spirits ceremonial packaging, fashion boxes and displays, watch and jewelry cases, gastronomy packaging, technology packaging, and corporate gifting objects.

AROS Group emphasizes precision engineering, sustainability-driven decisions powered by AI and data, and a global manufacturing network that ensures consistency. It highlights Ecovadis recognition for responsible processes and certified materials, positioning luxury as a harmony with the planet rather than a compromise.
